compatibility_policy: Canonical failure and symptom IDs and the activation boundary are append-only; preserve legacy aliases and deprecate instead of renaming or deleting IDs used by completed versions.

failure_families.definition: Failures between source acquisition and the final model-ready input, label, mask, or weight tensors.
Failures in the model representation, architecture, capacity, trainable parameterization, or mathematical objective, assuming model-ready tensors are correct.
Failures in how a correct model and objective are optimized over correct tensors, including schedule, order, budget, transfer, and update dynamics.
Failures introduced at inference time by context assembly, memory, retrieval, tools, workflow, generation policy, or output adaptation.
Failures in cases, scorers, verifiers, sandboxes, statistics, selection, or evaluation evidence that make measurement untrustworthy.
Execution failures that do not intentionally change scientific semantics, including environment, hardware, integration, orchestration, services, and artifacts.
Failures of permission, approval, budget, compliance, security, change control, auditability, or promotion policy.
A temporary holding family used only when evidence cannot yet localize the first broken invariant.

failure_modes.definition: A required source is absent or cannot be acquired.
Source bytes or encoding are damaged before ingestion.
The source version, origin, or immutable identity cannot be established.
The loader parses source syntax or encoding incorrectly.
Loaded fields, types, units, or required values violate the dataset contract.
Conversation roles or task fields are assigned to the wrong semantic roles.
Records from multiple sources are joined to the wrong identities or targets.
Examples contain irrelevant, malformed, or low-signal content.
The canonical target itself is factually or procedurally wrong.
A training example lacks required supervision.
Multiple valid targets are incorrectly represented as one unqualified target.
Training examples impose mutually incompatible supervision without an explicit conditioning variable.
Whitespace, indentation, or line endings are changed before the canonical target is frozen.
Unicode normalization or full-width and half-width conversion changes semantics.
Unit, date, currency, locale, or numeric formatting is normalized incorrectly.
Equivalent logical examples serialize to unstable or semantically different canonical text.
A training template adds, removes, reorders, or rewrites canonical target content before tokenization.
The wrong tokenizer or token-boundary handling changes model-ready supervision.
Label tokens are shifted or associated with the wrong input positions.
The intended mask policy is not faithfully materialized in labels, such as required tokens becoming -100.
Length handling removes required input or target tokens.
Padding enters the loss or valid tokens are masked as padding.
Packed examples leak across boundaries or lose sample separation.
A correct conceptual loss policy is converted into incorrect per-token weights.
Required domains, capabilities, or failure modes are absent or materially under-covered.
Class or label frequencies distort learning relative to the target population.
The composition of domains or skills does not match the intended learning objective.
Filtering, synthetic generation, or selection systematically excludes important examples.
The distribution of example quality is unsuitable despite individual labels being valid.
Exact duplicates inflate apparent dataset size or update weight.
Near duplicates create hidden overweighting or optimistic evaluation.
Evaluation content or equivalent answers enter training data.
Known benchmark material contaminates training or adaptation sources.
A sample identifier resolves to different content or multiple records.
Training examples differ materially from the target domain.
Training information is stale relative to the target time period.
The serving input distribution differs from training in an unmodeled way.
Training and inference templates induce different input or output distributions despite each being internally valid.
Tokenizer vocabulary or special-token semantics are incompatible with the model parameters.
Embedding parameters do not correspond to the intended tokenizer or representation.
The model representation cannot express the required context length or positions.
The model lacks a suitable representation for an input or output modality.
The output representation is structurally unsuitable for the required task contract.
The architecture's structural assumptions are poorly matched to the task.
The chosen component topology cannot support the required computation.
Attention connectivity or mechanism prevents needed information flow.
Routing assigns inputs to inappropriate components or experts.
Specialist boundaries or composition are mismatched to the skill structure.
The output head cannot represent or calibrate the required prediction.
Overall parameter capacity is insufficient for the target behavior.
Shared parameters create an information or adaptation bottleneck across tasks.
Usable contextual memory is insufficient despite valid input construction.
A domain-specific component lacks adequate capacity.
The selected base checkpoint lacks prerequisites or is poorly matched to the target domain.
Initial parameter tensors are damaged or internally inconsistent.
The initialization is too distant from the target domain for the permitted adaptation regime.
Parameters necessary for the behavior change are not trainable.
Adapters are attached to modules that cannot express the needed update.

The selected trainable layers exclude critical transformations.
The wrong specialists or experts are trainable.

Conceptual weights across tokens, samples, domains, or objectives are inappropriate.
Loss reduction or normalization changes the intended relative contribution of examples.

Supervised fine-tuning is the wrong objective for the desired behavior.
The preference objective does not encode the desired ranking or behavior.
A reward signal incentivizes proxy behavior instead of the intended outcome.
The KL or reference-model constraint is too weak, too strong, or semantically misplaced.
Simultaneous objectives impose incompatible gradients without a valid resolution policy.
Model-level regularization is insufficient to prevent overfitting or unstable specialization.
Model-level regularization suppresses required adaptation.
Dropout configuration is inappropriate for the adaptation regime.
Weight-decay semantics or scope are inappropriate for the model recipe.
A structural or parameter constraint prevents the intended behavior.
Static quantization loses information required by the target behavior.

A previously demonstrated capability declines.
Performance declines in a specific domain while other domains may improve.
An intervention produces no measurable improvement.
Qualification or ranking changes materially across seeds.
Generated output violates a required byte, token, or structural boundary.
Output fails the declared format contract.

Output repeats content or enters a generation loop.
The response cannot complete because a tool call or tool result is invalid.
A source, canonical, or model-ready data invariant fails.
Training and evaluation identities or content overlap unexpectedly.
Training loss or another optimization signal diverges.
NaN or infinite values occur during training.

Previously learned behavior is not retained after later updates.
Equivalent evaluation inputs yield inconsistent results.
Evaluation artifacts disagree in identity, type, hash, ordering, or content.
A candidate output cannot enter or complete sandbox execution.
Execution fails before meaningful model optimization or inference begins.

The causal or operational record is insufficient to reconstruct a decision.
A precommitted resource or access budget is exhausted.

intervention_crosswalk_examples.selection_note: Choose the representation leaf that repairs the first broken rendering invariant; masking is a dependent lever only when the repaired token would otherwise remain outside loss.

The failure name does not prescribe a fix: select one lever according to whether evidence localizes the missing retention signal to exposure, order, constraints, update magnitude, duration, or parameter scope.
Use these only after model-ready labels and masks have passed; bad label construction is a data-supervision failure, not a loss-formulation failure.
First distinguish base-model capacity from adaptation-scope capacity; changing architecture requires a goal that explicitly authorizes model.architecture.

case_examples.title: Canonical Code indentation was removed before loss construction
case_examples.last_good_stage: canonical assistant target in the materialized training dataset
case_examples.broken_invariant: Every Code nonmasked label sequence must begin byte-for-byte with the canonical four ASCII spaces.
causal_chain: All 105 canonical Code targets retained the required four-space prefix.
The pinned native training template applied assistant content.strip() and removed that prefix.
The ignore-empty-think loss path additionally masked the adjacent indentation boundary from the active labels.
Under the defective supervision, Code execution eligibility fell from Base 7/8 to 0/8 at late v0001 checkpoints and then plateaued.
Changing only target representation and the necessary balanced mask exchange restored eligibility to 8/8 at every v0002 Probe checkpoint.
